_what_this_is: A worked mapping manifest for a newsroom that does not exist. Every table, column and value is invented. It is here to show the shape of a complete answer, not to be copied: your warehouse is not Riverbend's, and a mapping copied from someone else's warehouse is the one artifact in this repository that cannot be reused. Check it with `engagement-kernel-lint-mapping examples/mapping --adapter-bundle examples/mapping/adapter`.
_why_no_gaps: Every field here resolves. A complete mapping is what you are aiming at, so the example shows one. The fourth outcome -- 'gap', for a field you cannot produce and cannot derive -- is shown in docs/agent-spec-1-map-your-warehouse.md instead, because an example whose job is to show a good answer should not also be the illustration of an unfinished one.

reader_id.rationale: The identity service's resolved-person key. Already one row per person, so the rename is mechanical -- but the filter beside it is not: identity.person also holds a row per anonymous browser, and shipping those would mint one contract reader per device.

id_grain.rationale: Constant 'resolved_person' for the rows that survive the resolution filter. Recorded as a derivation rather than a rename because the constant is only true given that filter; the source column it depends on is what makes it true.

event_id.rationale: The event stream's own primary key, unique across the stream.

reader_id.rationale: The same identity key as the registry, so the referential-integrity check the validator runs is a real check rather than a coincidence of naming.

event_ts.rationale: Stored UTC and emitted UTC, unconverted. A rename rather than a derivation on purpose: converting it to the declared day boundary here would apply that shift twice, since the engine applies it as well, and the second application is invisible.

channel.rationale: Riverbend's four surfaces collapse onto the contract's two: ios and android are both 'app', web and amp are both 'web'. A collapse loses the distinction between them, which is acceptable here because no feature in the engine reads it.

event_kind.rationale: Constant 'content_delivery' for rows that reference an article. The event stream holds no other kind that the contract has a value for, so rows without an article are dropped rather than mapped to something adjacent.

content_id.rationale: The CMS article key, joinable to the content table. Nullable in the contract; here it is never null because rows without one are filtered out upstream of the export.

session_id.rationale: Riverbend's warehouse has no sessions at all. Cut on 30 minutes of inactivity per reader, which is the threshold their existing dashboards already use -- choosing a different one would put the kernel's session counts at odds with every number the newsroom already trusts, for no stated reason.

engagement_time_seconds.rationale: Heartbeat count times 15 seconds, which is measured attention. Explicitly NOT the wall-clock gap between events, which counts the lunch break a reader left the tab open through. Zero heartbeats becomes null, not 0: null means unmeasured and 0 would mean arrived and read nothing.

content_id.rationale: The CMS primary key, the same key the event stream references.

content_type.rationale: Riverbend's templates map onto the contract's content types. Templates with no counterpart become 'other' rather than being dropped: the article-view definition selects which types count, so a type that exists and is not selected is a different statement from a row that is not there.

section_resolution.rationale: 'resolved' when the CMS section tag is set, 'unresolved' when it is not -- about 4% of articles. The tempting fix is to fill those with the site default, which would attribute a twentieth of all reading to a section nobody chose.

sections.rationale: A one-element list, because Riverbend's CMS permits exactly one section per article. The contract's list type allows several and the fractional attribution that goes with them; a publisher with one section per article simply never exercises it.

published_ts.rationale: First publication, not last update. An updated article is not a new one, and using the update timestamp would make an old article look freshly published every time a typo was fixed.

reader_id.rationale: The identity key again. Riverbend's billing system was migrated onto it in 2024, which is why the coverage floor on subscription history is where it is.

state.rationale: Eleven billing statuses onto the contract's seven states. The judgement calls: past_due and unpaid both become 'grace' because both are still-entitled dunning states at Riverbend; refunded and chargeback both become 'cancelled'; comped becomes 'active' because a comped reader has full access. Which of the seven are ENTITLED is not decided here -- that is scored_population, and it has a different owner.

payer_type.rationale: 'individual' for consumer plans, null for institutional and gift plans. Riverbend cannot distinguish who pays on those, and the contract's null means unknown. Writing 'individual' would convert a known unknown into a false known.

start_ts.rationale: Interval start, inclusive, matching the contract.

end_ts.rationale: Interval end, exclusive, null while the span is still open. The validator refuses overlapping spans and more than one open span per reader, which caught two genuine duplicate-row defects in the billing log on the first run.

event_id.rationale: The ESP's own click id. Unique per click, not per campaign-recipient pair.

reader_id.rationale: The ESP identifies subscribers by its own hash, so this joins through a mapping table. Rows whose hash does not resolve are dropped rather than pointed at a placeholder reader: an unresolved click belongs to somebody the rest of the delivery has never heard of. The drop rate is about 2% and worth monitoring, because if it climbed, email engagement would fall for a reason that is not about readers.

event_ts.rationale: UTC from the ESP, emitted unconverted for the same reason as the reading events.

list_id.rationale: The newsletter the click came from. Carried through rather than collapsed, so the engine can scope cadence to particular lists without a second delivery.

campaign_id.rationale: The individual send. Nullable in the contract and occasionally null here, for clicks on evergreen automated emails that Riverbend's ESP does not treat as campaigns.

availability.statement: Riverbend's ESP has an open feed, but open tracking was only enabled in June 2026, part-way through the analysis period. Declaring it available with a coverage floor was considered and rejected: the floor mechanism handles a window that starts before the input existed, and the intended first run reaches back further than that, so every window would drop the block anyway. Revisit once a full year sits after the enablement date.

Riverbend closed comments in 2019 and runs no events, no forum and no reader submissions. There is no source to map, now or later, so this is 'not_deployed' rather than 'not_yet_launched' -- the distinction matters because not_yet_launched drops the block only for windows that reach back past a floor, and there is no floor here to reach past.
